subject: Intermittent cross-VPC session drops — suspected NAT/route-priority conflict
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@evergreenbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@evergreenbank.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent session resets to Redwood private deployment (VPC-peering)

Marissa —

We started seeing intermittent application session resets to the Redwood deployment in our prod VPC after the maintenance window. The behavior looks like short (2-15s) drops and then sessions re-establish; affected flows are primarily TLS connections from our app servers to the inference endpoint (10.10.20.0/24 -> 172.31.45.0/24).

What we've collected so far:
- Traceroutes from two app hosts (attached: evergreen_traceroute_0507.txt)
- A small pcap showing repeated SYN/ACK retransmits and mid-connection RSTs (attached: evergreen_pcap_sample_0508.pcap)

This started ~03:00 UTC on 2026-05-07, correlates with a change on our side where we enabled a new NAT gateway for egress (per cloud provider change). Can you triage? We have a live incident bridge open if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Senior Cloud Ops, Evergreen Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Thanks Alex — looping in Dev and Hannah from Infra/Networking. Quick ack from us: we see TCP retransmits in the pcap but need more context (VPC route tables, NAT behavior, and whether any ECMP/AS-path changes happened).

Initial asks (please provide if available):
- Host-level mtr/traceroute to the inference endpoint from an affected host during an incident window
- VPC route table snapshots, specifically routes to 172.31.45.0/24 and any custom route priority entries
- NAT gateway config (are there multiple NATs, are they behind LB/ECMP)
- Any recent BGP/peering changes with transit or partner (timestamps around 03:00 UTC)

We'll start by checking edge ALB/peer NAT timeout and MTU assumptions on our side. I'm assigning this as high priority.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@evergreenbank.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent session resets to Redwood private deployment (VPC-peering)

Quick update from infra side after an initial look at the pcap:
- The pcap shows repeated SYN/ACK retransmissions and then a RST originating from our edge (172.31.45.37) shortly after the retransmit series.
- No obvious MTU blackhole in the samples provided (we see MSS ~1420 agreed and packets of expected size).
- However, our VPC peer table shows two potential overlapping routes to the customer network: a direct peering route and a transit route via a partner router. Priority is currently ambiguous: route selection may be flipping and is likely causing asymmetric return paths which can break TCP state if NAT mapping isn't sticky.

Action items I'm initiating:
1) Force-route pinning on the peering attachment for Evergreen to prefer direct peering for a 60-minute window (will revert after we confirm stability).
2) Enable detailed VPC flow logs for the affected subnet for 2 hours and share exports.
3) Request customer to move a small test flow to port 8443 so we can correlate ALB logs and flow logs simultaneously.

Alex — any chance you can run the following from one affected app host and paste results?
- ip route show
- iptables -t nat -L -n -v (if applicable)
- ifconfig | grep -i mtu

I'll follow-up with a short recap to the war-room.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Dev —

Thanks for the quick triage. Per your asks, here are the outputs from host app-12 (snippet attached in evergreen_traceroute_0507.txt):
- ip route shows our default egress via NAT-GW-A with a more-specific route to 172.31.45.0/24 via peering-attachment-3
- iptables NAT table has a source-NAT rule pointing at NAT-GW-A (we did add a second NAT gateway during maintenance, but traffic should be pinned via the more-specific route)
- ifconfig: MTU on host is 1500

One additional detail: our cloud provider introduced a change to how they announce peering prefixes to transit partners around 03:00 UTC (they called it a "peering adjacency optimization"). We flagged it in the provider's support portal.

We're happy to test port 8443 as suggested. Standby for confirmation window.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@evergreenbank.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent session resets to Redwood private deployment (VPC-peering)

Folks — post pinning the direct peering (Dev's action) and after Evergreen switched the test flow to 8443, we observed the following:
- No further RSTs or SYN/ACK retransmit bursts in the next 45 minutes for test flows, sessions remained stable.
- VPC flow logs show symmetric routing when the direct peering is preferred; when the transit path is selected we saw asymmetric flows and NAT mappings dropped after ~12s of inactivity which matches symptom windows.

Conclusion: root cause appears to be route selection oscillation between direct peering and transit (likely due to provider's new adjacency optimization). NAT mapping was not sticky across the asymmetric return path which caused TCP connections to be reset.

Next steps / asks:
- Evergreen: ask your provider to open an incident referencing the adjacency optimization and request they fix announcement ordering for the peering prefix. Please push any provider ticket ID into JIRA:NET-789.
- Redwood: we will add a persistent route preference for Evergreen's peering attachment and add a short-term health check that prefers direct peering while provider works the fix.
- Both: schedule a 30-min postmortem next week to review mitigations (MTU checks, NAT pinning, route-preference hardening).

I've attached our internal troubleshooting checklist (redwood_debug_checklist.pdf) and the sample pcap for reference. If Evergreen needs an SLA credit conversation because this crossed impact thresholds, loop in Sales/Account execs — I'll coordinate.

Thanks everyone for the fast collaboration.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
